templates.prompt: Use Green's theorem to evaluate ${∮}_{C}({e}^{x}-2{x}^{2}y)\,dx+({e}^{y}+2x{y}^{2})\,dy,$ where $C$ is the boundary of the triangle with vertices at $(0,0),$ $(2,2)$ and $(-2,2),$ traversed counterclockwise.
templates.worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](images/7c/7ca4b6fe3a5a16c4004c75b0e4524cc3b42550cb2413d5b8e1c21a1d53cee902.png)

We have that $P(x,y)={e}^{x}-2{x}^{2}y$ and $Q(x,y)={e}^{y}+2x{y}^{2}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=-2{x}^{2},\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x} & =2{y}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the region $D$ as a type II region as follows:

$$
D={(x,y):-y\le x\le y,\,0\le y\le 2}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's Theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}({e}^{x}-2{x}^{2}y)\,dx+({e}^{y}+2x{y}^{2})\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2{y}^{2}+2{x}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{-y}^{y}(2{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2})\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}2{[\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}+x{y}^{2}]}_{-y}^{y}\,dy \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{2}(\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}+{y}^{3}+\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}+{y}^{3})dy \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{8{y}^{3}}{3}\,dy \\  & =\frac{16}{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}{y}^{3}\,dy \\  & =\frac{4}{3}{[{y}^{4}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}\cdot {2}^{4} \\  & =\frac{64}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

![](images/00/007634ca34871f05cde9d44a58fcf24b1e5fd3b8c337c68f2025fb8724eef819.png)

First, notice that we can rewrite our integral as follows:

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot dr={∮}_{C}(6{x}^{2}-xy+11)\,dx+({y}^{2}+1)\,dy
$$

We have that $P(x,y)=6{x}^{2}-xy+11$ and $Q(x,y)={y}^{2}+1.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=-x,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the region $D$ as a type I region as follows:

$$
D=\{(x,y):0\le x\le 2,-\frac{x}{2}\le y\le \frac{x}{2}\}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's Theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}(6{x}^{2}-xy+11)\,dx+({y}^{2}+1)\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}[0-(-x)]\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}x\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{-x/2}^{x/2}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}x[y]_{-x/2}^{x/2}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}x(x)\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{2}\,dx \\  & ={[\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{8}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](images/39/3954846460076fa1ef1e5826d32bde9145e7350cb2324072b001d8c6ff41cc14.png)

We have that $P(x,y)=xy$ and $Q(x,y)=2{x}^{2}+y.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=x,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x} & =4x.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the region $D$ as a type I region as follows:

$$
D=\{(x,y):-1\le x\le 3,\,0\le y\le 2\}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's Theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}xy\,dx+(2{x}^{2}+y)\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(4x-x)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}3x\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}3x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{3}3x[y]_{0}^{2}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{3}3x(2)\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{3}6x\,dx \\  & =3[{x}^{2}]_{-1}^{3} \\  & =3[9-1] \\  & =24.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](images/cb/cb85e51584f0c41fc19210a5ce56289baa652aff3046d5d88c034d187b7e45dd.png)

We have that $P(x,y)=2xy-{y}^{2}$ and $Q(x,y)={x}^{2}+2x.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=2x-2y,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x} & =2x+2.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the region $D$ as a type I region as follows:

$$
D=\{(x,y):-1\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1-x\}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's Theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}(2xy-{y}^{2})\,dx+({x}^{2}+2x)\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2x+2-2x+2y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2+2y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}(2+2y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{[2y+{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{1-x}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}(2(1-x)+(1-x)^{2})dx \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}({x}^{2}-4x+3)\,dx \\  & ={[\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}-2{x}^{2}+3x]}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =[\frac{1}{3}-2+3]-[-\frac{1}{3}-2-3] \\  & =\frac{2}{3}+6 \\  & =\frac{20}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
